extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical and life-science researchers (postdoctoral applicants) preparing an application for the HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program
extracted.subtask_short: HHMI Hanna H. Gray fellowship application
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and requirements for applicants to the HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program, an up-to-8-year fellowship supporting outstanding early-career scientists through mentored postdoctoral training and a faculty-phase transition, with emphasis on scientific excellence and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection is of outstanding early career scientists who have demonstrated: a commitment to making foundational discoveries; building an inclusive culture in academic science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching purpose against which candidates are evaluated — applicants should show both scientific ambition toward foundational discoveries and concrete actions/commitment to improving inclusion in academic science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Stage Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have been accepted to join a lab in the U.S.; have no more than 24 months of postdoctoral research experience at the time of application due date; hold a PhD and/or MD (or equivalent) which is conferred by the start of the grant term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are strict eligibility requirements — applicants must verify acceptance to a U.S. lab, ensure their postdoc experience does not exceed 24 months as of the deadline, and confirm degree conferral by grant start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit 75% of total effort to research in a postdoctoral training position by the grant start date; commit to a minimum of two years of postdoctoral training in this position after the grant start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must plan for and document the required minimum time/effort commitment (75% effort, ≥2 years postdoc in the specified position) in mentor letters and career plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / Degree Location Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to all; non-U.S. citizens and applicants with other nationalities must have a degree from a research institution in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although citizens of any country may apply, international applicants must hold a degree from a U.S. research institution — ensure this is clear in application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Research Disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition is open to those dedicated to basic research from doctoral and/or medical training paths in the biomedical and life science disciplines (examples: plant biology, evolutionary biology, biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, computational biology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets basic biomedical/life-science research; applicants should demonstrate their work fits within these disciplines and emphasize basic-research aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with Program Structure / Phase Readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Program has Phase 1 (postdoctoral phase, up to 4 years: mentored research, career development, publication) and Phase 2 (faculty phase, up to 4 years: continued support upon transition to faculty, resources to launch independent lab, mentoring and community).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should present a plausible plan for success during the mentored postdoc period and a credible trajectory for transition to an independent faculty position to take advantage of Phase 2 support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record of research accomplishment; quality of proposed research project; potential to make foundational discoveries; letters of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes past productivity and rigor (publications, achievements), the scientific significance and rigor of the proposed project, and external validation via letters — all indicating high potential for foundational contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to develop independent research program; compelling research vision; potential to lead an independent lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for evidence that the candidate can articulate and pursue an independent, coherent research agenda distinct from prior mentors, and has the leadership potential to run a lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated commitment to making academic science more inclusive; mentorship history; diversity, equity, and inclusion activities; personal narrative on diversity contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong applications include concrete examples of past DEI/mentoring activities, a thoughtful personal statement about contributions to inclusion, and plans to cultivate inclusive culture in future scientific leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and ambition; feasibility within fellowship period; match between candidate skills and proposed work; choice of host laboratory and mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed research should be innovative yet realistically executable within the fellowship timeframe; reviewers assess alignment of candidate expertise with project goals and the suitability of the mentor and lab environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Application Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Research statement (proposed work); personal statement (career trajectory + DEI commitment); three letters of recommendation; mentor's commitment letter; diversity statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents are required and must collectively demonstrate scientific promise, a credible career plan, mentor support, and substantive DEI engagement — prepare each to speak directly to the selection criteria above.
